title: Multiplicative simply connected covering of a semisimple algebraic group
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $H$ be a semisimple $F$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. There exist a semisimple simply connected $F$-group scheme $\widetilde H$ and a multiplicative isogeny $\pi:\widetilde H\to H$ with central kernel. Here a semisimple group is a smooth connected affine group scheme of finite type with no nontrivial smooth connected solvable normal closed subgroup scheme; solvable means that its successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial. Simply connected means that every surjective homomorphism $H_1\to\widetilde H$ from a semisimple group scheme $H_1$ with finite central scheme-theoretic kernel is an isomorphism. A multiplicative isogeny means a homomorphism whose pullback on coordinate algebras is faithfully flat and whose scheme-theoretic kernel is finite and of multiplicative type. Faithfully flat means that extension of scalars is exact and detects zero modules. Finite means having finite-dimensional coordinate algebra. A finite group scheme is of multiplicative type if, after extension to an algebraic closure, it is diagonalizable: it is isomorphic to $D(M)=\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ for a finite abelian group $M$, with comultiplication $e_m\mapsto e_m\otimes e_m$ on the group-algebra basis. Central means commuting with every group element after every scalar extension. The trivial semisimple group is allowed.

source.place: Theorem 18.25 and Remark 18.27, printed p.393; Definitions 18.5 and 18.7, printed pp.388--389; Lemma 19.14 and Proposition 19.15, printed pp.400--401. A universal covering is a multiplicative isogeny; its source is semisimple by 19.14.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-picard-trivial-multiplicative-cover] to the smooth connected affine finite-type group $H$. Obtain a smooth connected $P$ and a multiplicative isogeny $\pi:P\to H$ with $\operatorname{Pic}(P)=0$. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-isogeny-invariance], $P$ is semisimple: the target $H$ is semisimple and the kernel of $\pi$ is finite. Put $N=\ker\pi$.

For $N\cong\operatorname{Spec}F[M]$ with $M$ finite, its characters are exactly the basis elements $e^m$: pullback of the coordinate $t$ of $\mathbf G_m$ is an element $a$ with $\Delta(a)=a\otimes a$ and $\varepsilon(a)=1$, and conversely such an element defines a character (its inverse is the image under the antipode). Apply [lem-sfb-group-algebra-group-like-basis]. Thus $X^*(N)\cong M$ is finite. This uses the affine spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and the displayed group law [def-sc-gm-ga], and applies to nonreduced $N$.

source.place: Lemma 12.4 and the evaluation formula following it, printed p.232.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-semisimple-characters-trivial], $X^*(H)=0$. The exact sequence [lem-sfb-character-picard-isogeny-sequence] for $\pi$ therefore makes restriction $X^*(P)\to X^*(N)$ injective. Its target is finite by step 2, whereas its source is torsion free by [lem-sfb-connected-group-characters-torsion-free]. Every element of the source has finite order by this injection, and hence is zero. Thus $X^*(P)=0$, in addition to $\operatorname{Pic}(P)=0$.

To check the stated simply connected condition, let $q:Q\to P$ be any surjective homomorphism from a semisimple $Q$ with finite central kernel $K$. By [lem-sfb-semisimple-central-isogeny-multiplicative], $q$ is multiplicative and faithfully flat. Apply [lem-sfb-character-picard-isogeny-sequence] to $q$. Since $X^*(P)=0=\operatorname{Pic}(P)$, restriction identifies $X^*(Q)$ with $X^*(K)$. The former is torsion free by [lem-sfb-connected-group-characters-torsion-free], and the latter is finite by the calculation in step 2 applied to $K$. Hence both groups vanish. Write $K=D(M_K)$ as supplied by multiplicativity: step 2 identifies $X^*(K)$ with $M_K$, so $M_K=0$ and $K=D(0)=1$ scheme-theoretically.

For every commutative $F$-algebra $A$, the base change $Q\times_P Q\to Q$ of $q$ is an isomorphism: the inverse to its second projection sends $x$ to $(x,x)$, since any pair $(y,x)$ with $q(y)=q(x)$ has $yx^{-1}\in K(A)=1$. The formulas are natural in $A$ and define inverse scheme maps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-isomorphism] with $h=q:Q\to P$ and $\varphi=q$: the cover is flat and surjective by step 4 and quasi-compact since it is a morphism of affine schemes. Therefore $q$ is an isomorphism. This proves the required simply connected condition on $P$.

source.place: Proposition 18.19, final implication; Corollary 3.35, printed p.75; Stacks 02L4 (lemma-descending-property-isomorphism).

proof.text: The identity of $H$ is a multiplicative isogeny (identity extension of scalars and trivial kernel $D(0)$). Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-isogeny-composition] to $\pi$ and this identity: its conclusion makes the kernel of $\pi$ central. Taking $\widetilde H=P$ now gives all clauses. The argument includes $H=1$; equivalently its cover can be the identity of the trivial group. No reducedness of either finite kernel was used.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 18.25, proof, through Propositions 18.22 and 18.18; Proposition 18.19 argument and Proposition 19.15; Lemma 19.14 proof. Descent of the final isomorphism uses Stacks 02L4.
